knowledge: State adversary capability/knowledge/position explicitly and declare out-of-scope; a weaker attacker must still motivate the work and a stronger attacker must not trivialize it.
fails_when: no identifiable threat model;internally inconsistent assumptions;undefined adversary knowledge

knowledge: Evaluate any adversarial-ML attack or defense against an ADAPTIVE, defense-aware adversary using the strongest correctly-tuned published attacks; no gradient masking.
provenance: Carlini & Wagner 2017; Athalye et al. 2018 obfuscated-gradients; 219-best-paper calibration
fails_when: no adaptive/defense-aware eval;gradient masking or obfuscated gradients unaddressed;static/transfer-only attack presented as robustness evidence

knowledge: Address the base-rate fallacy, split datasets temporally with no future leakage, and report false-positive cost at deployment scale.
provenance: Arp et al., Dos and Don'ts of ML in Computer Security, USENIX'22
applies_when: ML detection;intrusion detection;malware classifier;anomaly detection;base rate;dataset split
fails_when: base-rate fallacy ignored;temporal leakage;false-positive cost at scale unreported

knowledge: Prove constant-time claims rather than asserting them; evaluate on real hardware and demonstrate end-to-end secret recovery, not just a distinguisher.
fails_when: constant-time asserted not proven;simulation-only;distinguisher without secret recovery

knowledge: Use a real testbed or hardware-in-the-loop and quantify the PHYSICAL consequence; simulation-only needs an explicit fidelity argument and control-loop timing must be respected.
fails_when: simulation-only without fidelity argument;physical consequence not quantified;control-loop timing ignored

knowledge: Match device/vendor diversity to the generality claim and identify a vulnerability CLASS rather than one vendor's bug; state the realistic attacker position and disclose with CVEs.
fails_when: single-device case study sold as general;root cause is one vendor bug;unrealistic attacker position;no disclosure

knowledge: Position any new signing/attestation/OTA scheme against in-toto, SLSA, TUF, Uptane, Sigstore and Notary, and name the exact pipeline point it protects.
best_practice: position vs prior attestation frameworks; state protected pipeline stage
fails_when: new scheme not positioned vs in-toto/SLSA/TUF/Uptane/Sigstore/Notary reads as a RENAME;protected pipeline point unspecified;threat model omits compromised-signer/rollback

knowledge: Validation is a PROOF (increasingly machine-checked), not an experiment; empirical work here is performance, not correctness.
fails_when: correctness argued by experiment instead of proof;proof soundness unaddressed

knowledge: Rule out that the finding is a measurement artifact via multiple vantage points, ground-truth validation and robustness to methodology choices; observe scanning ethics/IRB.
fails_when: finding could be a measurement artifact;single vantage point;no ground truth;scanning ethics unaddressed

knowledge: Carry a coordinated-disclosure narrative with dates/CVEs/embargo; ethics adequacy is judged, not mere presence, and IRB approval is not a safe harbor.
provenance: security_paper_conventions.md ethics section; USENIX Ethics Considerations policy
fails_when: undisclosed exploitable vulnerability with no plan;vague disclosure timeline;boilerplate ethics naming no stakeholders

knowledge: A taxonomy/definition must have lineage to an established one (adopt+cite or extend), never a self-invented scheme with no provenance; note CCS does not accept SoK.
fails_when: self-invented taxonomy with no lineage where a standard exists;named category presented as novel

knowledge: Connect the work to real CVE and MITRE ATT&CK when a relation genuinely applies; use verifiable canonical ids (CVE-YYYY-NNNNN on NVD; Txxxx/Txxxx.yyy in the stated ATT&CK version, ICS matrix for CPS/OT) and only mappings that truly hold.
best_practice: verifiable CVE/ATT&CK mapping when applicable; state absence honestly
provenance: cve_attack_mapping.md; MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise/ICS matrices; NVD/CVE List
applies_when: CVE;MITRE ATT&CK;technique mapping;tactic;threat landscape;vulnerability id;ATT&CK for ICS
fails_when: fabricated or non-resolving CVE;wrong or forced ATT&CK technique id;self-coined technique without matrix lineage;detached ATT&CK appendix with no in-text argument

knowledge: Pre-register the method, evaluation plan and numeric success criteria before running experiments; every reported number must trace to the frozen plan. Moving a success criterion, metric or threat model after seeing results is HARKing, not a finding.
best_practice: freeze success criteria before running (pre-registration); results cite the frozen plan
provenance: open-science pre-registration norm; AAR (Chen Yueh-Han et al. 2026) results-free frozen mini-paper §3.2; research_loop iron rule #3
applies_when: experiment design;success criteria;pre-registration;threat model set at design;metrics chosen;HARKing
fails_when: success criterion or metric moved after results seen;threat model reverse-engineered so the attack works;reported number not traceable to a pre-registered plan

knowledge: Report across the full evaluation set (all testbeds/datasets/devices/targets) with regressions disclosed, keep a held-out that method development never touches, hold utility at or above baseline, and report the seed distribution rather than the best single run.
best_practice: no cherry-picking across benchmarks; untouched held-out; utility non-regression; seed distribution not best run
fails_when: only favorable subset of benchmarks reported;hyper-parameter tuned on the reported test set;best single run reported as the result;utility regression below baseline hidden
